title: Independent AI review of product continuation after software acquisitions
method: A separate OpenAI Codex agent used the existing product roster, public source links, anchors, two-year follow-up and shipment rule. It read dated source materials, searched for supplementary primary evidence and recorded its first-pass outcomes for all 29 lines before inspecting the original row-level outcome values or explanations. It then compared the two sets and examined the disputed boundaries. The original overlap codes, case intake and primary-source selection were not independently rebuilt. Source discovery was shared; this was an AI-assisted reconstruction, without blinded independent human raters. The comparison tests classification of this roster, not completeness or empirical truth.
scope: All 29 roster lines were assessed for shipment and business-level authority context. The four case histories give detailed timing and conditions for control. The remaining authority notes identify the operating or ownership context at the selected date and are not full governance audits.

codebook.shipment: Dated primary evidence of a material capability available to intended users, a live trial, or a completed deployment of the named line or a traceable successor.
codebook.activity: An existing service, maintenance or use without a verified in-window shipment. Actual shipment status remains unknown.
codebook.cessation: Positive evidence documenting termination of the named service.
codebook.unresolved: Insufficient dated evidence even to classify activity or cessation.
codebook.authority: The operating entity, original/substitute owner and documented consent arrangements at the evidence date. A purchaser, public spokesperson or regulator is a release signatory only if a source specifically assigns that decision. An airline, police force or practice may decide to adopt a release without controlling the supplier’s next release.

comparison_summary.interpretation: Agreement measures the four-state outcome, irrespective of date or which event establishes shipment. Dates are evidence dates or event months and need not be first releases. Reconciliation applies the published product-boundary rule to both readings. It supplies no independent accuracy estimate, causal estimate or reliability statistic for authority.

chronology: FNZ acquisition anchor.

CMA initial enforcement order, reissued November 22. The order required separate operation, resources for pre-merger development plans and preservation of ordinary-course management responsibilities. Departures specified in the order needed prior written CMA consent.
GBST reported customer upgrades to the new cloud Composer version.
Interim order continued separate operation and protection of development resources.
GBST reported a bank’s completed migration to its latest Composer release. Client identity was withheld.
End of window.
Sale to Anchorage completed. Composer was in the wealth-management business retained by Anchorage. The capital-markets division followed a different path.
gbst.who_could_act: GBST management operated the separate business under the order. FNZ held legal title. The CMA could consent to specified departures. The evidence supports that allocation at the business level.
gbst.unknown: GBST CEO Robert DeDominicis publicly described the client upgrades. His comments and the orders do not identify who approved either release, the payment authorizer, or a release-specific derogation.

chronology: Dye & Durham acquisition anchor.
CMA initial order required separate operation, development resources and ordinary-course management. The CMA varied the order on September 30, 2021.
CMA final report required sale.
TM Group and CDS reported that additional AP1 filing features were available to users. Final undertakings were still at proposal stage.
CMA accepted final undertakings pending disposal.
End of window.
Aurelius acquisition completed.
tmgroup.who_could_act: TM Group remained the separately operated supplier during the release. Its parent was subject to the CMA order. CMA consent was reserved for specified departures.
tmgroup.unknown: The trade outlet published the target’s account and named product manager Joanna King. It establishes her product role and live functions. It does not establish unilateral sign-off by King, Dye & Durham, a monitoring trustee, HM Land Registry or the CMA.

farelogix.unit: FLX NDC distribution and FLX Merchandise rules engine
chronology: Sabre–Farelogix abandonment anchor.
Accelya announced completion. Farelogix CEO Jim Davidson was appointed chief product officer of the enlarged group and the announcement described management integration.
Hawaiian and Accelya identified previously deployed FLX Merchandise and the Open Connect/NDC implementation underway.
Air France-KLM announced its agreement for FLX Merchandise. The trial described in this announcement was prospective.
Accelya said the teams, brand and product portfolios had been integrated.
Accelya confirmed Hawaiian’s HA Connect distribution implementation had launched. Hawaiian’s own presentation identified the Farelogix NDC API.
End of window.
farelogix.who_could_act: At the dated product observations Accelya held corporate authority. Davidson had a documented group product remit. Hawaiian could authorize adoption and use in its own distribution channels.
farelogix.unknown: These records do not show whether Davidson, another executive or a committee approved the next vendor release or which commitments came from a customer. Launch of distribution does not demonstrate a new shipment of the rules engine.

chronology: CMA initial order required separate operation and pre-merger development resources, subject to the specified consent route.
viagogo acquisition anchor.
CMA required sale of StubHub International.
CMA records completion of the sale to Digital Fuel.
Purchaser identified the UK as part of the carve-out and Wayne Grierson as StubHub International general manager. Its announcement described the live resale marketplace.
End of window.
stubhub.who_could_act: The separate StubHub operation was protected during the order. Following divestiture, the UK business operated under StubHub International management and Digital Fuel ownership. US and Canadian operations were excluded.
stubhub.unknown: The announcement gives no product change, release decision or individual approval. A new owner or a continuing marketplace leaves the shipment outcome unknown.
